narrative:
The model determined that you have a 51% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is just over the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and the type of property you own. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the denial. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This situation pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Your credit history of “no credits or all paid” was the second most important factor. This is quite rare—only 1% of applicants share this history—whereas 57% of approved customers have a clean record of existing credits that were paid on time. This also increased the likelihood of being seen as a bad risk.

The fact that you own real estate worked in your favor and was the third most influential piece of information. It pulled the prediction back toward approval, but not enough to overcome the other two factors.

Your relatively low loan amount and short duration were positive signals, yet they carried less weight than the checking account and credit history.

To improve your chances next time, focus on building a positive credit history with this bank and bringing your checking account balance into positive territory before reapplying. These two steps will remove the largest obstacles the model identified.
